name: Larkspur
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Larkspur, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Larkspur, CA: the chamber tree lighting, Santa and Nutcracker storytime at Marin Country Mart, and The Polar Express at the Lark Theater.
lede: Larkspur keeps Christmas close to its historic downtown and to Larkspur Landing, with a chamber tree lighting, Santa and storytime at Marin Country Mart and a restored Art Deco theater that screens holiday films.
celebrates: The Larkspur Chamber of Commerce and the Town of Larkspur share a calendar of annual events, and the holiday tree lighting is one of them. The chamber's page promises more than 50 trees lit at once, pictures with Santa, hot drinks, caroling and a bonfire, and local sponsors can register to sponsor a tree. At Larkspur Landing, Marin Country Mart adds its own tree lighting, a Nutcracker Storytime with Marin Ballet, Photos with Santa and a Giving Tree gift drive run with Side by Side. Downtown, the Lark Theater adds a family movie night built around a holiday classic.
lastyear: In 2025 the Larkspur Chamber of Commerce listed Holiday Magic Happens, Tree Lights in the Park, with the same promise it makes today: more than 50 trees lighting up all at once, with Santa, hot drinks, caroling and a bonfire. The chamber's page for that event started the gathering at 4 pm and carried it until dusk, when the trees were lit. The event has become the chamber's yearly kickoff for the season, held in partnership with the Town of Larkspur.
facts: Larkspur was incorporated in 1908, according to the Larkspur Chamber's history page. Larkspur City Hall at 400 Magnolia Avenue was dedicated on April 20, 1913, with a parade of schoolchildren, speeches and the baptism of a baby. The Lark Theater, an Art Deco cinema built in 1936, was slated for demolition in 2003 before neighbors mounted a Save the Lark campaign, and it reopened as a nonprofit on July 9, 2004, with 205 seats.
trains: Trains and boats meet at Larkspur Landing. The SMART Larkspur station connects to the Golden Gate Ferry, and SMART runs a Connect Larkspur shuttle that links the station, the ferry terminal and the surrounding Larkspur Landing area. The ferry terminal opened in 1976 on the site of the old Hutchinson's Rock Quarry. For a train day in the city, San Francisco has three train museums, listed below, and the Lark Theater's holiday screening of The Polar Express adds a North Pole train for little riders.
train_links: See the giant wheels that pull San Francisco's cable cars, free to visit on Mason Street.
A small free museum of streetcars and cable cars at the foot of Market Street.
The nonprofit behind San Francisco's historic streetcars on the F line.
traditions: The chamber's tree lighting in Larkspur Community Park, with over 50 trees lit at once, Santa, hot drinks, caroling and a bonfire.
Businesses and neighbors can register through the chamber to sponsor a tree in the park.
Marin Country Mart's gift drive with Side by Side, where shoppers pick a tag, buy a present and return it unwrapped.
Marin Ballet brings Act I of The Nutcracker to life with costumed storytellers and dancers at the Mart.
The Lark Theater invites families to wear pajamas to a holiday film with hot chocolate and cookies.
kidfact: Larkspur's Lark Theater was nearly torn down in 2003, until neighbors started a Save the Lark campaign and brought it back.
faq: What is there for kids at Christmas in Larkspur?

Larkspur's season centers on a chamber tree lighting with Santa pictures, a Marin Country Mart tree lighting and Nutcracker Storytime, Santa photos at the Mart, and a pajama screening of The Polar Express at the Lark Theater. Each event page lists exact dates, times and prices where they are printed.

Larkspur Landing is where the Golden Gate Ferry terminal, the SMART Larkspur station and Marin Country Mart sit together. The ferry terminal opened in 1976 on the former Hutchinson's Rock Quarry. The SMART Connect Larkspur shuttle links the station, the terminal and the surrounding area.
Can we get to Larkspur by train?

Yes. SMART serves the Larkspur station, and the SMART site says riders can make connections to San Francisco by taking the Larkspur ferry from that station. The Connect Larkspur shuttle also meets every southbound train at the Larkspur station within 10 minutes, so families can ride on to the ferry terminal.

The Lark Theater is a single screen Art Deco cinema on Magnolia Avenue, built in 1936. It was restored by local residents after a Save the Lark campaign and reopened on July 9, 2004, as a nonprofit community film and culture center with 205 seats.
